newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia tobacco magnate confirms stake in Astra.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia tobacco magnate confirms stake in Astra.

text.p: Indonesian tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna confirmed on Monday that he had bought 9.81 percent of Astra International, the country's biggest carmaker, in two weeks of frenzied trading of the group's stock.

Sampoerna, who controls cigarette company Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna and is one of the wealthiest men in the country, said in a letter to the stock market regulatory agency Bapepam that he had bought the stake as an investment.
Copies of the letter were released to the press by Bapepam.
Astra shares were trading at 3,800 rupiah on Monday afternoon, up from 2,625 two weeks ago. The shares have been rising constantly since then on rumours that a takeover bid was in progress.

An Indonesian newspaper has said members of President Suharto's family are also interested in building up stakes in Astra. It named his eldest daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana and his sons Bambang Trihatmodjo and Hutomo Mandala Putra as prospective buyers.

The Bisnis Indonesia daily has said Rukmana, who controls toll-road operator Citra Marga, is in talks with timber magnate Prajogo Pangestu, Astra's largest shareholder, to buy out his 10.68 percent stake.
It has also said Sampoerna may sell his holdings to a group controlled by another timber tycoon Bob Hasan.
Neither report has been independently confirmed but Bapepam said on Monday that Pangestu still held his original stake.
Hasan's Nusamba group is owned 80 percent by three foundations controlled by Suharto himself.
The president's eldest son Sigit Hardjojudanto and Hasan hold ten percent each.
Brokers have said buying a stake in Astra would be beneficial to both Trihatmodjo and Mandala Putra, who own separate joint ventures with South Korean vehicle manufacturers.

Mandala Putra is the sole beneficiary of Indonesia's controversial national car policy, which grants his company tax and tariff breaks subject to meeting local content requirements within three years.
Trihatmodjo, who heads the Bimantara group, has also requested similar tax breaks but the government has said only one company will get the benefit for at least three years.

Brokers say Astra's production and distribution base would be useful for either. They also see potential for synergy with Rukmana's toll-road operations as Astra is likely to bid for contracts to build Jakarta's elevated suburban train system.
Astra's holdings are widely held. After Pangestu and Sampoerna, the next largest chunk of shares is held by Japan's Toyota Motor Corp with 8.26 percent.
